subject: Flowlane upsell: commit restructure and rate threshold alignment
messages:
From: Alex Chu <alex@flowlane.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@flowlane.com>, Elena Park <elena@flowlane.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Flowlane renewal: committing to higher hosted API baseline

Marcus —

As we get closer to our October renewal, execs want to lock in a higher monthly baseline for the hosted API. We had another month of growth (25% MoM on token volume) and would like to move from our current 1.5M token commit to a 3.5M token monthly baseline.

High-level asks:
- Can you send a draft amendment that shows unit pricing at the new commit tiers and the burst/overage treatment?
- We need a clear rate-limit/soft-throttle threshold per minute and per-second that won’t break our production SLAs.
- Procurement wants an expected lead time for a PO and any legal/SC redlines to expect.

Would appreciate a one-page mutual action plan so we can present to finance next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chu
Head of Engineering, Flowlane
alex@flowlane.com
(415) 555-0182

---
Attachment: Flowlane_usage_q2.csv (reference)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chu <alex@flowlane.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Flowlane renewal: committing to higher hosted API baseline

Alex —

Really appreciate the heads-up and congrats on the growth. I pulled together a short proposal and a draft amendment (attached) that outlines:
- New monthly commit: 3.5M tokens
- Unit price tiers: baseline unit pricing (per-1k tokens), plus stepped discounts above 4M and 8M
- Burst allowance: 25% of baseline per month for short spikes; overage billed at our standard overage rate unless you opt into a burst pocket option (we can show numbers for a fixed monthly buffer)
- Soft-throttle thresholds: 20 requests/second per API key with a sustained 120 reqs/minute guardrail; automatic graceful degradation to model-variant fallback if sustained exceedance happens for >5 minutes

I attached a one-page mutual action plan and a draft amendment (commit_amendment_v3.docx). Karthik is looped to confirm the rate-limit wording and ops implications.

Next steps I propose:
1) Your procurement teams reviews the draft and flags any legal/econ redlines
2) We finalize numbers and push to DocuSign by end of next week
3) PO + payment processing; we can provision the increased capacity on the first invoice cycle after signature (we typically need 7 business days for provisioning and validation)

Let me know if you want to set up a 30-min call tomorrow with Karthik to walk the traffic model and the throttles.

—
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0120

Attachment: commit_amendment_v3.docx

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal:
- Procurement asks whether the burst allowance is refundable or simply an accounting buffer.
- Legal wants to avoid open-ended auto-billing for overages. Can we add a notification + manual approval step at $5k over monthly spend?
- On rate-limits: our traffic pattern is very spiky (short bursts at 250 reqs/sec for 30–90s during batch inference windows). Will the soft-throttle/variant fallback be transparent enough to our SREs (headers, error codes) so we can detect and failover gracefully?

If you can add a short appendix to the amendment describing the notification flow and the error codes/headers, that would help our integration testing.

Alex

Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2029 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Flowlane renewal: committing to higher hosted API baseline

Alex —

Great questions — quick answers and what's in the amendment appendix: 

1) Burst allowance: it's an accounting buffer (non-refundable). If you consistently need the burst pocket we recommend converting that into a permanent increased commit or adding a paid burst pocket (fixed monthly fee) — both options are shown in commit_amendment_v3.docx.

2) Overages: we can absolutely gate automatic billing. We will:
   - Send an automated spend alert at 60% and 90% of budgeted monthly spend
   - Hold any overage billing >= $5,000 for manual approval (Procurement will receive a notice with one-click approve/decline links)

3) Rate-limits & SRE visibility: Redwood returns structured headers and clear HTTP 429s with a JSON payload that includes:
   - error_code: RATE_LIMIT_SOFT or RATE_LIMIT_HARD
   - current_rps and sustained_window_seconds
   - suggested_retry_after_seconds or fallback_model_id when model-variant fallback occurs
We also emit tracing hooks to your tracing endpoint and can add a short webhook to post real-time throttle events to a Slack channel or ops webhook for your SRE team.

Operational note: given your 250 rps burst windows, we recommend adding a short-lived burst pocket (1M tokens/month) for Q4 to avoid repeated fallback events while we observe patterns. We can provision the pocket immediately after contract signature.

If you're ok, Dylan can set up a 30-min runbook review and a short test harness call to validate headers in staging.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: runbook_throttle_headers.txt (sample headers + error payloads)
